correctness.rationale: All quantifiers and normalization are fixed: n interior nodes, n+1 arbitrary positive lengths, unit diffusion and homogeneous Dirichlet; M_ii=(h_i+h_(i+1))/3 and K_i,i+1=-1/h_(i+1). Exact diagonal dominance and Schur complements imply adjacent coefficients stay strictly positive for tau>0. Usmani tridiagonal inverse identity then produces a negative distance-two entry for every positive offdiagonal of M+tau K. This proves necessity, while the Stieltjes inverse argument gives sufficiency including equality. n<=2 is handled separately. A standalone Fraction-based solver passed 618 rational tests, which do not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: The assessed novelty is an exact necessary-and-sufficient positivity cutoff for every positive nonuniform Dirichlet interval mesh with at least three interior nodes, not the already-known sufficient Stieltjes bound. The new backward implication follows from an unconditional strict adjacent-entry lemma and explicit negative two-hop witnesses. Full-text material for Li--Huang (2012) and Schatz--Thomée--Wahlbin (2010) supplies the closest broader numerical-analysis comparisons; their displayed theorems provide sufficient criteria or nonuniform small-step obstructions, not this all-mesh equivalence. value.rationale: The result closes the logical gap between known sufficient M-matrix timesteps and their necessity in one dimension on any fixed graded Dirichlet mesh. Its explicit sharp cutoff is independent of the boundary cell sizes, and it settles the minimal-grid distinction n=2 vs n>=3. This guides positivity-preserving time-step choice for arbitrary spatial grading and provides a falsifiable sharp benchmark; it is a complete natural class, not an arbitrary finite slice.
